troposphere.label: Clouds and weather, all of it, from here up
Ordinary birds, near the top of their range
Insects and "aerial plankton" lifted on rising air
Bar-headed geese — they fly higher than almost any other bird
Airliners cruise near the top of this layer, around 10–12 km

stratosphere.label: Weather balloons climb this high before they burst
The ozone layer, absorbing ultraviolet light
Bacteria and fungal spores, carried this high by chance

mesosphere.label: No birds, no insects — meteoroids burn up as meteors instead

karman-line.label: The conventional line between sky and space

low-earth-orbit.label: Thousands of active satellites share this region
Crewed and uncrewed spacecraft pass through on their way further out

iss.label: A continuously inhabited outpost, orbiting every 93 minutes

animal-astronauts.label: Fruit flies — the first animals sent to space
Laika, the first animal to orbit Earth
Mice, frequent research passengers aboard the ISS
Bees, tested for flight behaviour in microgravity
Zebrafish, studied for how bones and muscles react to weightlessness
Tardigrades — able to survive the vacuum of space directly

space-debris.label: Inactive satellites, still in orbit long after they stopped working
Spent rocket stages, left behind after launch
Fragments as small as flecks of paint, moving fast enough to matter

inner-van-allen.label: Energetic particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field — not a solid thing, a field

outer-van-allen.label: A second, larger belt of trapped particles further out

deep-space.label: Mostly nothing — the emptiness is the point
Occasional dust and rock, drifting for millions of years

solar-wind.label: A continuous stream of charged particles, flowing outward from the Sun

moon-approach.label: The Moon grows from a point of light to a visible disc

moon.label: Footprints that will outlast almost everything built on Earth
Landers, rovers and equipment, left where they stopped
